Brookland, DC. By way of Burlington and Dublin.

I'm a marketing communications specialist studying at Champlain College, with a minor in entrepreneurship and a semester in Dublin behind me. I've built email campaigns for more than 6,000 congressional staff at the U.S. House of Representatives, run a bi-weekly B2B bulletin through HubSpot, and owned a weekly employee newsletter for two years straight.

I founded Key Era and The Kalimba Collective, which means I've also learned the parts nobody teaches — how to book talent, hold a budget, and get people into a room on a Thursday night.

Most of my work sits where writing meets production. Someone has to decide what the thing says, and someone has to make sure it ships on Tuesday. I like being both people.

Featured strategy

Can a brand be an activist if it still has to sell something?

Black + Forth is Angel Gregorio's all-Black vendor marketplace on Channing Street NE. I audited it and found the harder problem under the good press: the activism isn't legible to Washingtonians, and the marketplace reads as an afterthought to The Spice Suite. Consumers know the spices better than the advocacy.

Three pillars answer it — reframing the spice business as the revenue engine that openly funds Black + Forth, taking the brand off the property through pop-ups and school visits, and giving "support Black-owned business" real meaning through one named policy issue a year.

It closes with a measurement framework across economic redistribution, community impact and civic engagement, plus a straight list of the risks: founder burnout, audience mismatch in a gentrifying city, and commercializing the mission itself.

Selected work

Putting a congressional office on social media, from zero

U.S. House of Representatives — Office of the CAO

A full launch plan for an office with no public social presence. Built the case on Pew data, wrote two audience personas, set platform-by-platform cadence for Instagram, X and Facebook, and drafted governance rules covering nonpartisan voice, accessibility and employee privacy. Includes a two-week Instagram content calendar, mock graphic and video posts, and first-year targets: 2,500–5,000 followers, 3–4 posts a week, 50 reels, 5% average engagement.

What I do

Four areas. Most projects touch more than one of them.

Analytical marketing

Campaign performance, open and engagement rates, segmentation, and reporting that turns a spreadsheet into a decision.

Internal communications

Staff newsletters and organizational messaging. Writing for people who didn't choose to subscribe, and keeping them reading anyway.

Social media marketing

Content calendars, channel strategy and on-brand creative across LinkedIn, Instagram and TikTok, built to a cadence you can sustain.

Event planning

Conference activations, run-of-show, tech riders and budgets. From the first booking email through to load-out.

HubSpot is where I work.

Full campaign cycles built in HubSpot — segmented B2B audience lists, automated email sequences, rebuilt CRM workflows so a team can see what's actually landing, and open and engagement reporting every cycle. It's the platform I know best and the one I'd bring to a new role on day one.
